mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods following a >0.5% decrease in FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods following a >0.3% increase in UNRATE (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies benefit from increased sales.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods following a sustained increase in RSAFS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods following a >1% decrease in INDPRO (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods meeting the trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals strong economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies benefit from increased economic activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and GDPC1 grows > 2% YoY
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods meeting the trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy and reduced corporate margins.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods following a >2% YoY increase in CPIAUCSL (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary environment combined with weak supply-side fundamentals, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods meeting the trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05).
